bibliographic.title: Artificial Intelligence Regulation: a framework for governance
bibliographic.authors: Patricia Gomes Rêgo de Almeida; Carlos Denner dos Santos; Josivania Silva Farias
bibliographic.citation_apa: de Almeida, P. G. R., dos Santos, C. D., & Farias, J. S. (2021). Artificial Intelligence Regulation: a framework for governance. Ethics and Information Technology. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10676-021-09593-z

methodology.method_family: systematic literature review and integrative framework development
methodology.study_design: systematic review of Artificial Intelligence Regulation (AIR) literature (2010–2020) combined with analytical synthesis into an integrative framework based on Design and Action Theory
methodology.sample_description: literature on Artificial Intelligence Regulation published between 2010 and 2020, including frameworks and guidelines organized around the framework concept
methodology.sample_size: 21 prior depictions of the policy-making process integrated
methodology.technology_context: general artificial intelligence and machine learning systems; public policy, legislation, and governance contexts

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article provides a conceptual integrative framework for AI regulation and governance based on a systematic review of AIR literature, which aligns with governance and regulated-context themes. However, the provided text addresses AI and machine learning generally and does not mention LLMs, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or operational conversational governance mechanisms specific to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage marked central_candidate, but full-text evidence shows no LLM or conversational-AI specificity; confirm whether generic AI regulation frameworks should be included as foundational context.

appraisal.notes: Objective and outputs are clearly stated, and the method family (systematic review plus integrative framework synthesis) fits the stated aim. Appraisal is limited by the excerpt: detailed search strategy, inclusion or exclusion criteria, quality assessment, and explicit limitations are not visible in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is coherently presented as an integrative synthesis of 21 prior policy-making depictions with a clear governance objective. Relevance to the target review is moderate-to-low because evidence concerns generic AI regulation rather than conversational or LLM-specific governance in regulated deployments.

coding.theme: Conceptual framework for artificial intelligence regulation and governance
model_layers: core functions for AI system development

synthesis.main_claim: The authors propose an integrative AIR framework for regulating AI across all stages of modern public policy-making, derived from a systematic review of AIR literature from 2010 to 2020 and synthesis of 21 prior depictions of the policy-making process.
synthesis.contribution: Offers a generic, country-specific, stakeholder-aware conceptual lens for deciding what, when, and how AI uses should be regulated, combining diverse theories and principles such as Agile and Ethics within Design and Action Theory.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on AI regulation and governance frameworks; not central evidence for LLM-based conversational governance because the text does not address conversational AI, LLMs, or deployment-specific operational controls.
